Document: Part 45 – Fixed Costs
Part 3 of 4
==================================================
## Fixed costs

## 45.45 .—(1) In Table 12—

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > 45.45 .—(1) In Table 12—] (a)unless stated otherwise, “damages”—

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > 45.45 .—(1) In Table 12—] (i)means any form of monetary relief;

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > 45.45 .—(1) In Table 12—] (ii)in a claim which has no monetary value, shall be taken to mean an amount equivalent to—

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > 45.45 .—(1) In Table 12—] (aa)£10,000 in a claim assigned to complexity band 2;

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > 45.45 .—(1) In Table 12—] (bb)£15,000 in a claim assigned to complexity band 3; and

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > 45.45 .—(1) In Table 12—] (cc)£20,000 in a claim assigned to complexity band 4;

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > 45.45 .—(1) In Table 12—] (iii)in a claim which includes both a claim for monetary relief and a claim which has no monetary value, means the applicable amount in sub-paragraph (ii) taken together with the monetary value in sub-paragraph (i); and

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > 45.45 .—(1) In Table 12—] (iv)in so far as it applies to monetary relief, means—

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > 45.45 .—(1) In Table 12—] (aa)agreed damages; or

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > 45.45 .—(1) In Table 12—] (bb)an amount awarded following trial;

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > 45.45 .—(1) In Table 12—] (Rule 44.2 provides that the court has a discretion as to the costs order to be made including whether an order for costs relating only to a distinct part of the proceedings is appropriate.)

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > 45.45 .—(1) In Table 12—] (b)the figures in each of stages A to C are the cumulative totals for costs incurred up to and including that stage;

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > 45.45 .—(1) In Table 12—] (c)the figures in stage D are separate sums where the claim is disposed of at trial; and

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > 45.45 .—(1) In Table 12—] (d)a reference to a ‘trial’ is a reference to the final hearing. ## Specialist legal advice

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Specialist legal advice] 45.46. —(1) Where a claim would normally be assigned to complexity band 4, under rule 26.15 in addition to the costs allowable in Table 12, the fixed costs may include an amount in accordance with Table 13. [PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Specialist legal advice] (2) The additional costs in Table 13 are only allowable where—

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Specialist legal advice] (a)the legal advice is obtained from, or a statement of case is drafted by—

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Specialist legal advice] (i)a specialist legal representative in respect of a matter within their specialist expertise; or

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Specialist legal advice] (ii)the intended trial advocate; and

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Specialist legal advice] (b)the use of that person to provide the advice or draft the statement of case is justified. [PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Specialist legal advice] (3) A court may only order payment for one advice in writing or in conference unless further advice is justified. [PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Specialist legal advice] (Rule 2.3 defines ‘legal representative’.)

## Advice obtained in claims started under the RTA Protocol or the EL/PL Protocol

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Advice obtained in claims started under the RTA Protocol or the EL/PL Protocol] 45.47 .—(1) This rule applies where a claim has been started under the RTA Protocol or the EL/PL Protocol. [PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Advice obtained in claims started under the RTA Protocol or the EL/PL Protocol] (2) Where this rule applies and—

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Advice obtained in claims started under the RTA Protocol or the EL/PL Protocol] (a)an advice has been obtained from a legal representative as provided for in the relevant Protocol; or

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Advice obtained in claims started under the RTA Protocol or the EL/PL Protocol] (b)an advice has been obtained from a specialist legal representative on the amount of damages where the claimant is a child and that advice—

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Advice obtained in claims started under the RTA Protocol or the EL/PL Protocol] (i)is within the legal representative’s particular expertise; and

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Advice obtained in claims started under the RTA Protocol or the EL/PL Protocol] (ii)is reasonably required to value the claim, the fixed costs may include an additional amount of £150. ## Preliminary issue or separate trial

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Preliminary issue or separate trial] 45.48. —(1) Where a costs order is made in favour of a party in respect of a preliminary issue, that party is entitled to the fixed costs in Table 12 for the stage applicable at the date the preliminary issue is concluded, together with such disbursements as are allowed in accordance with Section IX of this Part. [PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Preliminary issue or separate trial] (2) Where a claim continues following the conclusion of a preliminary issue and a costs order is made in favour of a party on conclusion of the claim, that party shall be entitled to—

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Preliminary issue or separate trial] (a)additional fixed costs, if it is the party in whose favour a costs order is made under paragraph (1); or

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Preliminary issue or separate trial] (b)fixed costs, if the party is not a party in whose favour a costs order is made under paragraph (1),

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Preliminary issue or separate trial] being in either case the amount specified for the stage in Table 12 within which the claim concludes, less the applicable amount in stage B(1), together with such disbursements as are allowed in accordance with Section IX of this Part. [PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Preliminary issue or separate trial] (3) Where the court orders a party to pay costs in respect of a preliminary issue, unless the court orders otherwise, those costs shall be paid within 14 days of the order. [PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Preliminary issue or separate trial] (4) Where, under this rule, a claim includes a claim for monetary relief and the court is unable at that stage to quantify the total fixed costs referred to in paragraph (1), the court—

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Preliminary issue or separate trial] (a)shall order the paying party to pay that element of the fixed costs which are specified in Table 12, as are then quantifiable, together with the applicable disbursements, unless there is good reason not to do so; and

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Preliminary issue or separate trial] (b)may order that party to pay a sum on account of that element of the fixed costs in Table 12 which are to be calculated by reference to a percentage of the damages to be awarded. ## SECTION VII Fixed Costs in the Intermediate Track

## Scope

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Scope] 45.49. —(1) This Section sets out the costs which are to be allowed in any claim which would normally be or is allocated to the intermediate track. [PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Scope] (2) This Section does not apply where Section IV, Section VI or Section VIII of this Part applies. ## Amount of fixed costs

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Amount of fixed costs] 45.50 .—(1) For as long as the case is not allocated to the multi-track, the only costs allowed in any claim which would normally be or is allocated to the intermediate track are—

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Amount of fixed costs] (a)the fixed costs in Table 14; and

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Amount of fixed costs] (b)the disbursements as set out in Section IX of this Part. [PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Amount of fixed costs] (2) In Table 14—

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Amount of fixed costs] (a)a reference to a date set by the court means the first date so set, notwithstanding that the parties may agree an extension to a later date, unless the court orders otherwise;

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Amount of fixed costs] (b)unless stated otherwise, “damages”—

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Amount of fixed costs] (i)means any form of monetary relief; or

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Amount of fixed costs] (ii)in a claim which has no monetary value, shall be taken to mean an amount equivalent to—

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Amount of fixed costs] (aa)£25,000 in a claim assigned to complexity band 1;

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Amount of fixed costs] (bb)£50,000 in a claim assigned to complexity band 2;

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Amount of fixed costs] (cc)£75,000 in a claim assigned to complexity band 3; and

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Amount of fixed costs] (dd)£100,000 in a claim assigned to complexity band 4;

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Amount of fixed costs] (iii)in a claim which includes both a claim for monetary relief and a claim which has no monetary value, means the applicable amount in sub-paragraph (ii) taken together with the monetary value in sub-paragraph (i); and

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Amount of fixed costs] (iv)in so far as it applies to monetary relief, means—

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Amount of fixed costs] (aa)agreed damages; or

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Amount of fixed costs] (bb)an amount awarded following trial;

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Amount of fixed costs] (Rule 44.2 provides that the court has a discretion as to the costs order to be made including whether an order for costs relating only to a distinct part of the proceedings is appropriate.)

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Amount of fixed costs] (c)the figures in each of stages S1, S3, S4, S5, S6 and S8 are the cumulative totals for costs incurred up to and including that stage;

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Amount of fixed costs] (d)the figures in stages S2, S7 and S9 to S15 are separate sums for those steps, if carried out; and

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Amount of fixed costs] (e)a reference to a ‘trial’ is a reference to the final hearing. [PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Amount of fixed costs] (3) The costs to be awarded for stage S1 are subject to assessment up to a maximum of the figure shown for stage S1 in Table 14, except in a claim for personal injuries where the figure shown is fixed. [PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Amount of fixed costs] (4) The costs in stages S2, S7 and S14 of Table 14 are only allowed where—

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Amount of fixed costs] (a)legal advice is obtained from, or a statement of case is drafted by—

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Amount of fixed costs] (b)a specialist legal representative in respect of a matter within their specialist expertise; or

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Amount of fixed costs] (c)the intended trial advocate; and

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Amount of fixed costs] (d)the use of that person to provide the advice or draft the statement of case is justified. ## Preliminary issue or separate trial

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Preliminary issue or separate trial] 45.51 .—(1) Subject to paragraph (3), where a costs order is made in favour of a party in respect of a preliminary issue, that party is entitled to the fixed costs in Table 14 for the stage applicable at the date the preliminary issue is concluded, together with—

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Preliminary issue or separate trial] (a)if there has been a trial, those fees appropriate in stages S8 and 9; and

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Preliminary issue or separate trial] (b)if appropriate, those costs specified in stages S2, S7, S9, S12, S13 and S14. [PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Preliminary issue or separate trial] (2) Subject to paragraph (3), where a claim continues following the conclusion of a preliminary issue and a costs order is made in favour of a party on conclusion of the claim, that party shall be entitled to—

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Preliminary issue or separate trial] (a)additional fixed costs, if it is the party in whose favour a costs order is made under paragraph (1); or

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Preliminary issue or separate trial] (b)fixed costs, if the party is not a party in whose favour a costs order is made under paragraph (1),

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Preliminary issue or separate trial] being in either case the amount specified for the stage in Table 14 within which the claim concludes less the amount in stage S3, together with—

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Preliminary issue or separate trial] (c)if there has been a trial, those fees appropriate in stages S8 and 9; and

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Preliminary issue or separate trial] (d)if appropriate, those costs specified in stages S9, S12, S13 and S14. [PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Preliminary issue or separate trial] (3) Only one set of fees can be recovered by any one party under stages S13 and S14 whether under paragraph (1) or (2). [PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Preliminary issue or separate trial] (4) The parties are entitled to disbursements allowed in accordance with Section IX of this Part incurred in any period for which costs are payable to them. [PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Preliminary issue or separate trial] (5) Where the court orders a party to pay costs in respect of a preliminary issue, unless the court orders otherwise, those costs shall be paid within 14 days of the order. [PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Preliminary issue or separate trial] (6) Where, under this rule, a claim includes a claim for monetary relief and the court is unable at that stage to quantify the total fixed costs referred to in paragraph (1), the court—

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Preliminary issue or separate trial] (a)shall order the paying party to pay that element of the fixed costs which are specified in Table 14, as are then quantifiable, together with the applicable disbursements, unless there is good reason not to do so; and

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Preliminary issue or separate trial] (b)may order that party to pay a sum on account of that element of the fixed costs in Table 14 which are to be calculated by reference to a percentage of the damages to be awarded. ## SECTION VIII Claims for Noise Induced Hearing Loss

## Scope

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Scope] 45.52 .—(1) This Section sets out the costs which are to be allowed in any claim for noise induced hearing loss which—

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Scope] (a)has been or should have been started under Annex E of the Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims; and

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Scope] (b)would normally be or is allocated to the fast track. [PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Scope] (2) Subject to rule 45.6(3), or unless a rule in this Section provides otherwise, the costs which are to be allowed are applicable to both claimants and defendants. ## Amount of fixed costs

## 45.53. —(1) The only costs allowed in any claim to which this Section applies are—

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > 45.53. —(1) The only costs allowed in any claim to which this Section applies are—] (a)the fixed costs in Table 15; and

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > 45.53. —(1) The only costs allowed in any claim to which this Section applies are—] (b)the disbursements set out in Section IX of this Part. [PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > 45.53. —(1) The only costs allowed in any claim to which this Section applies are—] (2) The cost of any additional pre-litigation advice is included within the Stage A costs and is not separately recoverable. ## More than one defendant

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > More than one defendant] 45.54. —(1) ) In Table 15, the reference to the number of defendants is to the number of active defendants against whom the claimant obtains a settlement or an award of damages. [PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > More than one defendant] (2) Where the defendants have all admitted liability and coordinate settlement between them, only one set of Stage 2 costs is allowed. [PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > More than one defendant] (3) Where at least one defendant admits liability and settles pre-litigation and at least one defendant denies liability—

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > More than one defendant] (a)the fixed costs payable by those defendants who have admitted liability are 100% of the stage 2A or 2B costs for those defendants as appropriate; and

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > More than one defendant] (b)Stage 3 and any subsequent stages shall apply to the remaining defendants, provided that the claimant must give credit for the costs already payable under (a), so that the maximum entitlement under any stage is for the applicable stage costs. ## Preliminary issues trials

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Preliminary issues trials] 45.55. Where the claimant succeeds at trial of a preliminary issue on limitation and an order for costs is made in favour of the claimant

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Preliminary issues trials] (a)the fixed costs may include those stages which would apply as if this was a trial of the claim, including trial advocacy fees; and

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Preliminary issues trials] (b)the claimant if successful in their claim for damages is entitled to additional fixed costs for the litigation stages only, starting with stage L2. ## SECTION IX Disbursements

## Scope of this section

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Scope of this section] 45.57 .—(1) This Section sets out the disbursements which are to be allowed in any claim to which Section IV, Section VI, Section VII or Section VIII of this Part applies. [PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Scope of this section] (2) Subject to rule 45.62, the court—

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Scope of this section] (a)may allow a claim for a disbursement of a type mentioned in rules 45.58, 45.59, 45.60 and 45.61, as applicable, and where it does so, the amount to be allowed is that which is reasonable and proportionate; but

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Scope of this section] (b)shall not allow a claim for any other type of disbursement. [PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Scope of this section] (3) Where appropriate, VAT may be recovered in addition to the cost of any disbursement allowable under this Section. ## Disbursements – Section IV

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Disbursements – Section IV] 45.58. In a claim to which Section IV applies, the court may allow a claim for a disbursement of a type mentioned in paragraphs (a) to (f)—

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Disbursements – Section IV] (a)subject to rule 45.62, the cost of obtaining—

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Disbursements – Section IV] (i)medical records; and

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Disbursements – Section IV] (ii)expert medical reports as provided for in the relevant Protocol;

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Disbursements – Section IV] (b)the cost of obtaining non-medical expert reports as provided for in the relevant Protocol;

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Disbursements – Section IV] (c)court fees payable—

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Disbursements – Section IV] (i)as a result of Part 21 being applicable;

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Disbursements – Section IV] (ii)where proceedings are started as a result of a limitation period that is about to expire; and

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Disbursements – Section IV] (iii)in respect of the Stage 3 Procedure;

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Disbursements – Section IV] (d)the provider cost of a telephone hearing;

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Disbursements – Section IV] (e)additionally, in a claim to which the RTA Protocol applies—

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Disbursements – Section IV] (i)an engineer’s report; and

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Disbursements – Section IV] (ii)a search of the records of—

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Disbursements – Section IV] (aa)the Driver Vehicle Licensing Authority; and

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Disbursements – Section IV] (bb)the Motor Insurance Database; and

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Disbursements – Section IV] (f)any other disbursement reasonably incurred due to a particular feature of the dispute or any requirement of these Rules. ## Disbursements – Section VI

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Disbursements – Section VI] 45.59. Subject to rule 45.15A, in a claim to which Section VI applies, the court may allow a claim for a disbursement of a type in mentioned in paragraphs (a) and (b)—

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Disbursements – Section VI] (a)in a claim started under a relevant Protocol to which Section IV applies—

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Disbursements – Section VI] (i)the applicable disbursements referred to in rule 45.58(a) and (b) and (d) to (f);

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Disbursements – Section VI] (ii)any court fees;

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Disbursements – Section VI] (iii)in a claim which arises from a road traffic accident, the cost of obtaining a police report;

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Disbursements – Section VI] (iv)any expert’s fee for attending the trial where the court has given permission for the expert to attend;

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Disbursements – Section VI] (v)any interpreters’ or translators’ fees;

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Disbursements – Section VI] (vi)expenses which a party or witness has incurred in travelling to and from a hearing or in staying away from home for the purposes of attending a hearing; and

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Disbursements – Section VI] (vii)a sum not exceeding the amount specified in Table 16 for any loss of earnings or loss of leave by a party or witness due to attending a hearing or to staying away from home for the purpose of attending a hearing; and

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Disbursements – Section VI] (b)in any other claim to which Section VI applies, any disbursement which has been reasonably incurred, other than a disbursement covering work for which costs are already allowed in Section VI. ## Disbursements – Section VII

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Disbursements – Section VII] 45.60. Subject to rule 45.15A, in a claim to which Section VII applies, the court may allow any disbursement which has been reasonably incurred, other than a disbursement covering work for which costs are already allowed in Section VII. ## Disbursements – Section VIII

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Disbursements – Section VIII] 45.61 .—(1) Subject to rule 45.15A, in a claim to which Section VIII applies, the court may allow a claim for a disbursement of a type mentioned in sub-paragraphs (a) and (b)—

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Disbursements – Section VIII] (a)the fees for the intended trial advocate for any step reasonably undertaken where both the use of that advocate and the cost are justified; and

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Disbursements – Section VIII] (b)any other disbursement which has been reasonably incurred. ## Soft tissue injury and whiplash injury claims

## 45.62. —(1) This rule applies—

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > 45.62. —(1) This rule applies—] (a)to a soft tissue injury claim; or

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > 45.62. —(1) This rule applies—] (b)a claim which consists of, or includes, a claim for a whiplash injury,

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > 45.62. —(1) This rule applies—] which arises from a road traffic accident. [PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > 45.62. —(1) This rule applies—] (2) Where this rule applies, the only sums (exclusive of VAT) that are recoverable in respect of the cost of obtaining a fixed cost medical report or medical records are as follows-

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > 45.62. —(1) This rule applies—] (a)obtaining the first report from an accredited medical expert selected via the MedCo Portal: £226;

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > 45.62. —(1) This rule applies—] (b)obtaining a further report where justified from an expert from one of the following disciplines—

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > 45.62. —(1) This rule applies—] (i)Consultant Orthopaedic Surgeon (inclusive of a review of medical records where applicable): £527;

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > 45.62. —(1) This rule applies—] (ii)Consultant in Accident and Emergency Medicine: £451;

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > 45.62. —(1) This rule applies—] (iii)General Practitioner registered with the General Medical Council: £226; or

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > 45.62. —(1) This rule applies—] (iv)Physiotherapist registered with the Health and Care Professions Council: £226;

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > 45.62. —(1) This rule applies—] (c)obtaining medical records: no more than £38 plus the direct cost from the holder of the records, and limited to £100 in total for each set of records required. Where relevant records are required from more than one holder of records, the fixed fee applies to each set of records required;

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > 45.62. —(1) This rule applies—] (d)addendum report on medical records (except by Consultant Orthopaedic Surgeon): £63; and

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > 45.62. —(1) This rule applies—] (e)answer to questions under Part 35: £100. [PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > 45.62. —(1) This rule applies—] (3) Save in exceptional circumstances, no fee may be allowed for the cost of obtaining a report to which paragraph (1) applies where the medical expert—

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > 45.62. —(1) This rule applies—] (a)has provided treatment to the claimant;

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > 45.62. —(1) This rule applies—] (b)is associated with any person who has provided treatment; or

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > 45.62. —(1) This rule applies—] (c)proposes or recommends treatment that they or an associate then provide. [PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > 45.62. —(1) This rule applies—] (4) The cost of obtaining a further report from an expert not listed in paragraph (2) is not fixed, but the use of that expert and the cost must be justified. [PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > 45.62. —(1) This rule applies—] (5) In this rule, ‘accredited medical expert’, ‘associate’, ‘associated with’, ‘fixed cost medical report’ ‘MedCo’, ‘soft tissue injury claim’ and ‘whiplash injury’ have the same meaning as in paragraph 1.1(A1), (1A), (10A), (12A), and (16A) and (20), respectively, of the RTA Protocol. ## Section X: Fixed Costs Determination

## Summary determination after hearing

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Summary determination after hearing] 45.63. —(1) Subject to paragraph (3), where the court makes an order for costs at the conclusion of a hearing, it shall in the absence of agreement between the parties make a summary determination of the amount of fixed costs or disbursements to which the receiving party is entitled in accordance with this Part. [PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Summary determination after hearing] (2) Any party who intends to claim any fixed costs or disbursements in accordance with this Part, must file at court and serve on any party against whom an order for payment is intended to be sought a completed Precedent U, which must include, if applicable, the details of any claim under rule 45.9, rule 45.10 or rule 45.13, no later than 24 hours before the time fixed for the hearing. [PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Summary determination after hearing] (3) Where a court is unable to make a summary determination at the conclusion of a hearing—

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Summary determination after hearing] (a)it may direct that the amount of fixed costs or disbursements be determined with or without a further hearing and may give such directions for the determination as it thinks fit; and

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Summary determination after hearing] (b)the costs of that determination shall be treated as if it were an interim application under rule 45.8. ## Determination where parties agree on all issues except costs

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Determination where parties agree on all issues except costs] 45.64. —(1) Where, in a claim to which this Part applies, the parties have reached an agreement made or confirmed in writing on all issues except the amount of costs or disbursements to be allowed under this Part, the receiving party may apply for the amount of those costs or disbursements to be determined in accordance with this rule. [PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Determination where parties agree on all issues except costs] (2) Where proceedings have been started, the application must be made in those proceedings under Part 23 as modified by this rule. [PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Determination where parties agree on all issues except costs] (3) Where proceedings have not been started, the application must be made by the commencement of costs only proceedings under rule 46.14 as modified by this rule. [PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Determination where parties agree on all issues except costs] (4) Save where the court directs to the contrary—

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Determination where parties agree on all issues except costs] (a)the evidence in support of the application must—

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Determination where parties agree on all issues except costs] (i)be served with the application; and

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Determination where parties agree on all issues except costs] (ii)include the written agreement or confirmation, together with a completed Precedent U containing details of the costs or disbursements to which the applicant claims to be entitled and, if applicable, the details of any claim under rule 45.9, rule 45.10 or rule 45.13;

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Determination where parties agree on all issues except costs] (b)any evidence in response to the application must be filed and served—

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Determination where parties agree on all issues except costs] (i)within 21 days of service of the application where proceedings have been started; or

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Determination where parties agree on all issues except costs] (ii)within 21 days of filing the acknowledgment of service where proceedings have not been started,

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Determination where parties agree on all issues except costs] and must include a completed response to the applicant’s Precedent U;

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Determination where parties agree on all issues except costs] (c)the application shall be determined without a hearing; and

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Determination where parties agree on all issues except costs] (d)the costs which the court may allow for the application are those set out in Table 17 in Practice Direction 45 and any appropriate court fee. [PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Determination where parties agree on all issues except costs] (5) The court shall record its determination of the application by annotating Precedent U with its decision noted against each item claimed, which must be served on the parties together with a notice stating that any party who wishes to challenge any aspect of the determination must file and serve a written request for a hearing. [PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Determination where parties agree on all issues except costs] (6) Any request for a hearing must—

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Determination where parties agree on all issues except costs] (a)be made within 21 days of service of the notice;

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Determination where parties agree on all issues except costs] (b)identify the decisions in the determination which the party wishes the court to reconsider; and

[PART 45 – FIXED COSTS > Determination where parties agree on all issues except costs] (c)provide a time estimate for the hearing,
